2. The respondent-petitioner was appointed as a driver on 1.6.77 by respondent No. 1, a Co-operative Society and was retired on 31.1.87 on completion of 57 years of age. The petitioner filed Dispute Case No. 21 of 1989 under section 86 of the Co-operative Societies Ordinance 1984 alleging that his date of was wrongly typed in his bio-data as 6.1.30 instead of 15.9.38. Respondent No. 1 contesting The ease stated that the petitioner did not mention his date of birth in his application for appointment but mentioned his age as 38 years. He furnished his bio-data on 7.12.77 in compliance with a direction from the respondent wherein he mentioned his date of birth as 6.1.30. The petitioner received his retirement benefit after his retirement. On consideration of his prayer for fresh employment on compassionate ground the petitioner was appointed on 19.5.87 on contract basis for one year on humanitarian ground. Thereafter he was employed for another year on contract basis. He accepted his retirement on and from 31.3.87 and waived his claim to challenge the order of retirement lie filed the Dispute Cast in 1989 mala fide creating papers subsequent, to retirement. His date of birth was recorded in the Group Insurance Policy as on 6.1.30 and premium was paid on that basis. 

 3. By order dated 25.5.89 the Arbitrator in the in Dispute Case passed an award in favour of the petitioner holding that his dale of birth was 15.9.38 and the date of his retirement would fall on 14.9.95. 

 4. On an appeal by the respondent the award of the Arbitrator was set aside by order dated 6.7.92 passed by the Deputy Registrar and Appellate Officer in Appeal Case No. 3 of 1992. 

 5. Thereafter the petitioner filed Miscellaneous Case No. 132 of 1992 before the learned District Judge, Dhaka under section 134(5) of the Co-operative Societies Ordinance, 1984 and by judgment and order dated 28.2.94 the 4th Court of Additional District Judge, Dhaka allowed the same and the order of the Appellate Officer was set aside. Being aggrieved by the same the employer-respondent moved the instant writ petition and obtained a Rule Nisi. 

 6. In his affidavit-in-opposition the petitioner reiterated his case that after the order of retirement he applied for correction of his date of birth producing certain documents which show that his date of birth was 15.9.38. 

 7. The High Court Division held that had the petitioner applied for correction of his age before his retirement then the documents produced in support of the same could have been considered but after his retirement from service there was no scope for correction of his age. The High Court Division also held that the petitioner received retirement benefits and served the respondent on contract basis for 2 years and thereafter tiled the dispute case. Hence he waived his right to challenge the validity of the order of retirement. The High Court Division also held that under section 134(5) of the Co-operative Societies Ordinance, 1984 the District Judge has been vested with the power to review the decision of the appellate authority. He is to see after examination of the records of the dispute case and appeal case whether the appellate authority acted illegally or with material irregularity in deciding the appeal causing miscarriage of justice. In a proceeding seeding of this nature there is hard any scope for examination of witness or production of documents afresh the fore him, which the learned Additions District Judge has done in disposing the miscellaneous case. He has acted it legally and with material irregularity in the exercise of his jurisdiction in no considering the materials relied upon by the appellate authority in passing the appellate order and in setting aside the same relying on fresh evidence adduced before him.
